keyframe_review.note: 32,048 km2 for 1803-1804: the electorate's outline with Osnabrück. The Kingdom page gives no area (the Westphalia page's 37,883 km2 for 1809 is a different state), so the comparison is not possible. The page: 'In 1803, Hanover was conquered by the French and Prussian armies in the Napoleonic Wars'; the French occupied the capital on 4 June 1803 and the Convention of Artlenburg of 5 July 1803 'disbanded the Electorate of Hanover' (Artlenburg page). The outline is kept for the land; the occupation is in the ledger.

correction.text: the electorate's outline of 1803, unchanged, held under French occupation: the Kingdom page's 'French control lasted until October 1813'

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria has no shape for 1805-1839. The outline of 1803 stays for 1805-1806 as occupied land (France since June 1803). The pages opened say nothing on 1805-1806 (no Prussian episode, no Hanoverian administration); the Kingdom page only says 'conquered by the French and Prussian armies' in 1803. Confidence 1 for the interval.

minus.text: the Hanoverian units the Westphalia page lists in 1807: the principalities of Göttingen and Grubenhagen 'with the enclaves of Hohnstein and Elbingerode', Goslar among the cities, Osnabrück among the principalities

correction.text: the 1803 outline less the Hanoverian units merged into Westphalia in 1807; the remainder still French-occupied

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: from 1807 the Hanoverian south goes to the Kingdom of Westphalia: 'created by Napoleon in 1807 by merging territories ceded by the Kingdom of Prussia' that include 'the territories of Hanover, Brunswick-Wolfenbüttel, and the Electorate of Hesse'. The page lists Göttingen, Grubenhagen, Goslar and Osnabrück among its units. The north (Lüneburg, Bremen-Verden) stays under French occupation until the annexation of December 1810, after which the whole realm is annexed and no keyframe is drawn for 1810-1812.

correction.text: 'George III was restored to his Hanoverian territories' (1813), the status quo of 1806

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: 'French control lasted until October 1813, when the territory was overrun by Russian Cossacks' and 'In 1813, George III was restored to his Hanoverian territories'. The Westphalia page: 'the status quo of 1806 was restored' on 26 October 1813, so the 1803 outline (without Hildesheim) is the shape until the Congress of Vienna.

correction.text: the kingdom of the Final Act: the former electorate plus East Frisia, Hildesheim, Lingen, northern Münster and Bentheim, without Lauenburg

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria's first postwar shape is 1840, which already shows the territory of the Final Act of 9 June 1815. The Congress page: 'The former Electorate of Hanover was expanded to a kingdom', gaining 'East Frisia from Prussia' and 'various other territories in Northwest Germany' and giving up Lauenburg to Denmark; the Kingdom page names Hildesheim, East Frisia, Osnabrück, the Lower County of Lingen, northern Münster, Bremen-Verden and Bentheim. The 1840 outline (38,269 km2, west to 6.68 E) is applied from 1815. Neither page gives an area.
38,269 km2: the post-1815 kingdom. No event on the pages explains the small difference between the 1840 and 1842 shapes (+219 km2, 0.6 percent); treated as digitisation.

38,488 km2 for 1842-1863: the kingdom's largest shape; nothing on the pages changes its border in these years (the page lists only the 1823 reorganisation into high-bailiwicks, which moves no frontier).
38,314 km2: 174 km2 less than 1842-1863 (0.5 percent) with no event on the pages; treated as digitisation. The border is unchanged until the 1866 annexation.
Same outline as 1864 (38,314 km2). Cliopatria's row ends here although the kingdom lasted to 20 September 1866.

correction.text: the 1865 outline, unchanged, to the annexation of 20 September 1866

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: the kingdom is annexed by Prussia on 20 September 1866 (infobox), so 1866 is its last year. The outline of 1865 is extended to 1866: 'Hanover: Annexed by Prussia, became the Province of Hanover'.

region.text: the electorate of Hanover with Osnabrück (Cliopatria outline of 1803)

ledger.note: 1803: the Hanoverian realm enters Cliopatria's 'Kingdom of Hanover' row, the electorate under George III, conquered that year by the French. 'In 1803, Hanover was conquered by the French and Prussian armies in the Napoleonic Wars.' The Kingdom page dates the kingdom itself to October 1814; 1803 is Cliopatria's boundary and the electorate dossier's hand-over year.

region.text: the Electorate of Hanover, its capital taken 4 June 1803, its army withdrawn north of the Elbe into Saxe-Lauenburg and forced to surrender

ledger.note: 4 June 1803: French troops occupy Hanover. The Artlenburg page: Napoleonic troops under Mortier 'occupied the electorate's capital at Hanover on 4 June 1803'; the Convention of 5 July 1803 'disbanded the Electorate of Hanover and instigated its occupation by French troops'. The occupier is the French Consulate, from 1804 the empire (first-french-empire), the counterpart string used for the whole occupation.

region.text: the Hanoverian units the Westphalia page lists in 1807: the principalities of Göttingen and Grubenhagen 'with the enclaves of Hohnstein and Elbingerode', Goslar among the cities, Osnabrück among the principalities

ledger.note: 1807: the Hanoverian south is merged into the new Kingdom of Westphalia. 'The Treaties of Tilsit in 1807 joined it to territories from Prussia and created the Kingdom of Westphalia' (Kingdom page); the Westphalia page names Göttingen, Grubenhagen, Goslar and Osnabrück among its units. The Hanoverian crown never ceded them; the 1813 events reverse the annexation. Land is my reading of the unit list.

region.text: the Aller department with its capital Hanover (Westphalian 1810-1813)

ledger.note: 1810: the rest of the Hanoverian realm is annexed by Westphalia and France. 'By the Westphalian and French annexations in 1807 and 1810' (Kingdom page); on the Westphalia page an Aller department with capital Hanover is listed for 1810-1813. The Aller department is the Westphalian share. [Reviewer eu-20-d, 2026-10-31: Hildesheim removed from the region: the Kingdom of Westphalia page lists Hildesheim among the territories ceded by Prussia in 1807, so it was not Hanoverian in 1810.]

region.text: the Nord (capital Stade) and Niederelbe (capital Lüneburg) départements

ledger.note: December 1810: the north is annexed by France. The Nord (capital Stade) and Niederelbe (capital Lüneburg) départements, 'coastal and northern', were 'ceded to the French Empire'. The page does not say that these are Hanoverian lands; Stade and Lüneburg are the Bremen-Verden and Lüneburg parts of the electorate (my reading).
December 1810: the French occupation of the north ends in annexation, drawn as the French empire's land (previous event). The Kingdom page: 'French control lasted until October 1813'.

region.text: the Hanoverian territories merged into Westphalia in 1807 and 1810

ledger.note: 26 October 1813: Westphalia falls and Hanover is restored. 'Prussian troops occupied Westphalia. The kingdom was then dissolved and the status quo of 1806 was restored'; 'In 1813, George III was restored to his Hanoverian territories' (Kingdom page).

region.text: the territory overrun by Russian Cossacks in October 1813

ledger.note: October 1813: the Hanoverian north is freed from France. 'French control lasted until October 1813, when the territory was overrun by Russian Cossacks.'

12 October 1814: the Electorate of Hanover is constituted as a kingdom. 'In October 1814, they were constituted as the independent Kingdom of Hanover at the Congress of Vienna'; infobox 'Congress of Vienna: 12 October 1814', in personal union with the United Kingdom 1814-1837. Same state, same colour (rule 2).
9 June 1815: Hanover gains East Frisia from Prussia. The Congress page: Hanover gained 'East Frisia from Prussia' and 'various other territories in Northwest Germany' (Final Act of 9 June 1815).

union.text: Lingen (Ems), the Lower County of Lingen; the gazetteer has no Lingen, so the circle is a placement at about 52.52 N 7.32 E
only the edge of the Münsterland region that Cliopatria's Hanover holds (by Lingen); the region itself is the Westphalian bay round Münster, the southern part of the bishopric, which became Prussian
the Prince-Bishopric of Osnabrück (a circle round the town)

region.text: Hildesheim, the Lower County of Lingen, the northern part of Münster, Bentheim and Osnabrück

ledger.note: 1815: Hildesheim, Lingen, northern Münster and Bentheim join the kingdom. The Kingdom page lists 'the Prince-Bishopric of Hildesheim, ... the Lower County of Lingen, the northern part of the Prince-Bishopric of Münster ... and the County of Bentheim' and gives no date or previous holder. The year is the Final Act's (Congress page, 9 June 1815); counterpart Prussia is my bridge (the Westphalia page says most of Westphalia 'became Prussian' in 1815). [fx-39, R112, 2 Nov 2026: 'Lingen' is not in the gazetteer, so this event was skipped as 'region does not resolve' and none of the 1815 gain reached the map. The place is now a 20 km disc at about 52.52 N 7.32 E (the coordinates the p1810-p1819 window gave for Lingen on the Ems; the Lingen and County of Lingen pages print none, and the County page says Lingen 'in 1815 became part of the newly founded kingdom of Hanover'). The Kingdom of Hanover page: Hanover increased its area 'gaining the Prince-Bishopric of Hildesheim, East Frisia, the Prince-Bishopric of Osnabrück, the Lower County of Lingen and the northern part of the Prince-Bishopric of Münster' and 'also annexed ... the County of Bentheim', without a date for the 1815 gain. Osnabrück is added because the page names it, and the Münsterland leaf is limited to Cliopatria's Hanover of 1840 (the page gives Hanover only 'the northern part' of Münster), as in the window's patch events/4, which this event now duplicates.]

region.text: the parts of Saxe-Lauenburg to the northeast of the Elbe

ledger.note: 9 June 1815: Hanover gives up Lauenburg. The Congress page: Hanover 'gave up the Duchy of Lauenburg to the Kingdom of Denmark'; the Kingdom page says it lost the parts of Saxe-Lauenburg northeast of the Elbe, 'assigned in personal union to Denmark'. [Reviewer eu-20-d, 2026-10-31: counterpart changed from denmark-norway (dossier ends January 1814) to kingdom-of-denmark-1814-1940, the Danish kingdom after the Treaty of Kiel.]

region.text: Hanover, invaded by the Prussian army on 15 June 1866, and the march south to Langensalza

ledger.note: 15 June 1866: the Prussian army invades Hanover. 'The Prussian Army invaded Hanover, Saxony and the Electorate of Hesse on 15 June'; Hanover had voted on 14 June for mobilisation against Prussia (Kingdom page).

About 29 June 1866: the Hanoverian army surrenders. 'Hanover's army defeated chaotic Prussians at the Second Battle of Langensalza on 27 June 1866', then was 'forced to surrender by superior numbers'; the timeline's 'Hanover surrenders two days later' gives about 29 June, not a stated date.

20 September 1866: Prussia annexes the kingdom. Infobox 'Annexed by Prussia: 20 September 1866'; Peace of Prague of 23 August 1866 (Austro-Prussian War page: 'Hanover: Annexed by Prussia, became the Province of Hanover').

20 September 1866: the Kingdom of Hanover ends; its land becomes the Prussian Province of Hanover. The church body formed on 19 September 1866, 'the day before the official Prussian annexation took place' (Kingdom page).

wars.name: French occupation of Hanover (1803)

zones.text: the Electorate of Hanover, occupied from 4 June 1803

wars.outcome: The Convention of Artlenburg (5 July 1803) 'disbanded the Electorate of Hanover and instigated its occupation by French troops'.
wars.note: Hanoverian troops 'withdrew north of the Elbe into the Duchy of Saxe-Lauenburg' and were forced to surrender; Wallmoden-Gimborn signed for Hanover.

wars.name: Napoleonic annexations of Hanover (1807-1813)
wars.outcome: Hanover is merged into the Kingdom of Westphalia (1807), the north annexed to France (December 1810); the status quo of 1806 is restored on 26 October 1813.
wars.note: Listed because the pages opened describe annexation by decree, not a campaign; no contest zone is drawn, the ledger's loss and gain events carry the land.

wars.name: Austro-Prussian War
wars.outcome: Hanover beats the Prussians at Langensalza (27 June 1866) but surrenders; 'Prussia annexes Hanover, Holstein, Schleswig, Hesse-Kassel, Nassau, Frankfurt'; the German Confederation is dissolved by the Peace of Prague (23 August 1866).
wars.note: Wikipedia dates the war 14 June to 22 July 1866; the Hanoverian army had already surrendered by about 29 June.

certainty.note: Occupation and annexation by the French, Westphalians and (per the electorate dossier) Prussians; the pages name units, not boundary lines.
Treaty borders from the Final Act of 9 June 1815 and the German Confederation; the Lauenburg and East Frisian frontiers are the treaty lines.

notes: ONE REALM, TWO CLIOPATRIA ROWS. The electorate-of-hanover dossier (another batch) ends the Electorate in 1802 and hands the realm to this dossier in 1803; this dossier therefore starts in 1803 (Cliopatria's boundary, confidence 1) and records the Kingdom proper as a rename in October 1814 (12 October on the infobox). Cliopatria has NO shape for 1805-1839 and ends in 1865, a year before the annexation of 20 September 1866 (infobox); new keyframes cover 1805-1806, 1807-1809, 1813-1814, 1815-1839 and 1866. NO KEYFRAME for 1810-1812: the pages describe the whole realm as annexed by Westphalia (south) and France (north), so the state holds no land; the ledger carries the 1807 and 1810 losses and the October 1813 gains, treated as annexations because the Kingdom page says 'the Westphalian and French annexations in 1807 and 1810'. THE PRUSSIAN EPISODE OF 1806 and the 1805 allied landing are on none of the five pages opened (budget); the Kingdom page's only mention is 'conquered by the French and Prussian armies' in 1803. The Osnabrück union of 25 February 1803 and the Prussian 1806 episode are in the electorate dossier's notes; this dossier cites neither. DISAGREEMENTS: the Westphalia page says the Aller department was Westphalian from 1810, while its prose says that only the north was ceded to France; the infobox area for Hanover is missing on every page opened. COUNTERPARTS: french-consulate and first-french-empire as occupiers (their dossiers belong to other batches/parts); 'denmark-norway' stands for the Danish crown after 1814 (Cliopatria's row for it is mis-dated; eu-14 owns it). NOT COVERED (page budget, five pages): the Treaty of Tilsit text, the 1815 Prussia-Hanover exchange treaty, the previous holder of Hildesheim, Lingen and Münster, Wangerooge and the 1853 Jade Treaty (the 1864 shape is 174 km2 smaller than 1842-1863 and no page explains it), Steuerverein. GAZETTEER NAMES NEEDED: 'East Frisia', 'Grubenhagen', 'Bremen-Verden', 'Lüneburg' (region), 'Saxe-Lauenburg', 'Münsterland', 'Bentheim'; 'Lingen' as a place.
